Subject: Quick recap + KMS/encryption topics we covered

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and next steps on the encryption questions you raised: 

- Scope: Acme Health will be sending PII (patient first/last name, DOB, limited addresses) to Redwood for inference in a hosted environment.
- Requirements called out on the call: in-transit encryption, at-rest encryption, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) option, audit logs for key usage, and the ability to limit retention of raw request payloads to 30 days.
- Action items we committed to:
  1) Share a succinct summary of our KMS options (Redwood-managed keys vs customer-managed KMS vs HSM integrations) and how each affects logging and retention.
  2) Provide a short diagram and an attachment with recommended controls for PII (masking, redaction, prefix caching rules).
  3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your security team (Rishi, Dev -- please propose availability).

I attached the initial requirements doc you sent (acme_encryption_requirements_v1.docx) and will follow up shortly with our KMS options doc.

Next step: I will send the KMS options doc by EOD tomorrow and Rishi will join the technical call if that works for Acme.

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before the technical deep-dive: 

- On customer-managed keys: we need to know if Redwood will have any way to access plaintext keys (NO), and whether keys can be rotated without downtime.
- For HSM: does Redwood support BYOK via an HSM provider, or edge HSM appliances for on-prem?
- Logs: we need a separation between access logs (who/what service requested tokens) and content logs (we prefer that raw request payloads be purgeable and optionally disabled for our account).

If you can include short, explicit answers to those items in the KMS doc that would be great. We can target next Wed for the security deep-dive (Jun 16) — please confirm availability.

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Legal Compliance <compliance@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KMS options + explicit answers (see attached)

Sam —

Attached is a short brief (redwood_kms_options.pdf) that covers our standard approaches and answers to your three bulleted questions:

1) Key access: Redwood does NOT have access to customer-managed KMS keys when you bring your own key. For Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored in our KMS and access is limited to automated signing for ciphertext at rest; no human access. We include per-request key-use audit logs.
2) Rotation: Customer-managed keys can be rotated in place without downtime for typical rotations (we use envelope encryption and key identifiers). For any key-material rotations that require re-wrapping, we provide a migration plan and a short maintenance window which we will coordinate with your team.
3) HSM/BYOK: We support BYOK via major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer HSM integrations for enterprise Private installs. For on-prem HSM appliances, we support both direct HSM-backed key wrapping and a hybrid mode where keys are kept on-prem and only metadata flows to Redwood.

Logging and retention:
- Access logs: preserved for 12 months by default; we can extend retention by agreement. Logs show key ID, timestamp, calling service, and request id.
- Content logs: raw request/response logging is disabled by default for workloads that opt-in; for accounts that enable it, Redwood supports configurable retention windows (you requested 30 days) and per-account purging. We also offer request-level redaction and prefix caching so stored KV cache entries do not contain full PII if you choose that pattern.

Attachments: redwood_kms_options.pdf (short comparisons + recommended default for Acme)

Next steps:
- Rishi/R&D: please confirm availability for Wed Jun 16, 10:00–11:00 PT for technical deep-dive with Acme security (Sam, Legal Compliance).
- I will add a short section to the drive doc about retention purge API and the audit log sample.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa

Subject: Internal: prepping for Acme security deep-dive (Wed)

Internal notes / tech prep (short):

- Confirmed: we support envelope encryption + customer KMS integration for hosted deployments. Behavior: user data encrypted at rest with a data encryption key (DEK) wrapped by CMK. Redwood services never persist unwrapped DEKs.
- For rotation, we support rewrap without downtime for most rotations; rewrap across regions may require brief coordination.
- HSM: for Private installs we can run with HSM-backed keys; for Hosted we support cloud-KMS BYOK (AWS/GCP/Azure). Need to validate with infra on on-prem HSM network requirements.
- Logging: add config notes on how to disable raw payload logs and enable only metadata access logs; prepare sample API snippet for purge / retention (30 days).

Action items:
- Rishi: prepare slide with architecture diagram (KMS flow + envelope encryption) + sample log entry format.
- Dev: prepare a short script and docs to demonstrate purge API and show that purge returns job id + completion timestamp.
- Marissa: confirm Wed 10:00 PT with Sam (I'll block the calendar once Rishi confirms).
